# `world/streaming/AdaptiveChunkBudget.js`

> **Source:** `engine/world/streaming/AdaptiveChunkBudget.js`

AdaptiveChunkBudget.js - Self-optimizing chunk memory management Uses PID-style control with EMA smoothing for smooth, responsive adaptation. Based on game engine best practices for adaptive performance.

## Classes

### `class AdaptiveChunkBudget`

AdaptiveChunkBudget.js - Self-optimizing chunk memory management Uses PID-style control with EMA smoothing for smooth, responsive adaptation. Based on game engine best practices for adaptive performance.

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `constructor()` |  |
| `setPageAllocator` | `setPageAllocator(pageAllocator, avgChunkMeshBytes = 1.5 * 1024 * 1024)` | Set limits based on GPU page allocator's detected VRAM Call this after GPUPageAllocator.init() completes |
| `setBufferPool` | `setBufferPool(bufferPool, detectedVRAM)` | Set limits based on GPU buffer pool (the actual mesh buffer allocator) This is more accurate than page allocator since it tracks real mesh memory |
| `getVRAMBasedJobLimits` | `getVRAMBasedJobLimits()` | Get VRAM-based job limits for ChunkJobCoordinator Scales with detected VRAM: 4GB=base, 8GB=2x, 12GB=3x |
| `shouldStopLoading` | `shouldStopLoading(currentChunkCount = 0)` | Check if we should stop loading chunks due to memory pressure |
| `adaptToVRAM` | `adaptToVRAM()` | Adapt chunk limit based on current VRAM usage Call this every frame - internally rate-limited |
| `recordFrame` | `recordFrame(frameTime, streamingTime)` | Record frame metrics - call every frame Uses EMA for smooth, responsive tracking |
| `getLimits` | `getLimits()` | Get current limits - call when checking chunk counts |
| `forceReduce` | `forceReduce(amount = 50)` | Force immediate reduction (emergency) |
| `getDebugInfo` | `getDebugInfo()` | Get debug info |

## Notes & Examples

### World Streaming & Scenes

The world system manages scene graphs, asset streaming, and level transitions. Scenes are entity hierarchies with spatial indexing (BVH) for fast culling and raycasts. Worlds stream assets asynchronously with priority based on distance and visibility.

**Example: Scene graph and streaming**
```js
import { World } from 'engine/world/World.js';
import { Scene } from 'engine/scenes/Scene.js';
import { Entity } from 'engine/ecs/Entity.js';

const world = new World();
const scene = new Scene();
world.addScene(scene);

// Create hierarchy
const player = new Entity('Player');
const camera = new Entity('Camera');
const weapon = new Entity('Weapon');

player.addChild(camera);
camera.addChild(weapon);  // Weapon follows camera

scene.add(player);

// Stream in a level
await world.streamLevel('level1', {
  priority: 'high',
  bounds: player.boundingBox,
  onProgress: (pct) => console.log(`Loading: ${pct}%`)
});

// Spatial query: find entities in radius
const nearby = scene.querySphere(player.position, 50);
```
